sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: Seven closed round trips reconciled to US$446 of gross trading P/L in the reviewed order-chain screenshots. The six short-put trades contributed US$417 and the separate short-call trade contributed US$29. This is a screenshot-based reconciliation, not a broker statement or independently audited track record.

sections.heading: Visual 1: Profit bridge
sections.body:
US$1,376 opening credits - US$930 closing buybacks = US$446 gross P/L.

Chart: opening credits in blue, buybacks in amber and gross profit in green. Label 32.41% as the proportion of opening credit retained, not return on account equity or return on margin.

sections.heading: Why close early?
sections.body:
The six puts captured 28.84% to 46.38% of their starting credit in approximately 27 to 50 hours. Buying them back crystallised US$417 of gross put gains and ended those positions' future assignment exposure. Pursuing the remaining US$719 of put premium would have kept downside and margin risk open.

The US$805 call was a separate, later trade and captured only 12.08% of its starting credit. It opened after the puts had closed. It must not be described as part of a simultaneous short-strangle position, and an uncovered short call can have unlimited upside loss.

sections.heading: Visual 3: Risk diagram
sections.body:
Eight short puts → 800 shares on full assignment → US$484,500 combined strike purchase obligation.

A hypothetical additional US$50 fall per assigned share → 800 × US$50 = US$40,000 further share-price loss.

Use three separately labelled boxes: assignment purchase obligation, broker margin requirement and discretionary downside reserve. Do not add them together as though they were the same thing.

sections.heading: Margin and evidence limits
sections.body:
The exact return on margin cannot be established from these screenshots. Historical peak broker buying-power reduction is missing. Do not use the earlier ten-put proposal's buying-power figure for the different executed trades, and do not add the later call's requirement to the puts' peak as though they overlapped.

These listed trades were already closed at the review date. Hypothetical hold-to-expiry figures are counterfactuals, not outstanding positions or promises of further income. Gross P/L excludes fees, financing and taxes not identifiable in the screenshots. Account balances and raw broker screenshots are not included in this public summary.

report.title: SPY short-put comparison: income versus assignment obligation
report.period_basis: Historical option snapshot and scenario analysis
report.provenance: Approved redacted summary of the dated private report. Original account evidence is not published.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: The higher-premium package carried a much larger purchase obligation. The two historical sell-to-open tickets compared one SPY US$700 put with ten SPY US$600 puts. They were order illustrations, not confirmed executions, and the maturities differed.

sections.heading: Visual 1: Side-by-side contract table
sections.body:
| Measure | Strategy A: one US$700 put | Strategy B: ten US$600 puts |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Expiry | 26 February 2027 | 31 December 2026 |
| Days shown on the original ticket | 115 | 58 |
| Assumed premium per share | US$12.19 | US$1.88 |
| Maximum gross premium | US$1,219 | US$1,880 |
| Shares if all assigned | 100 | 1,000 |
| Gross assignment obligation | US$70,000 | US$600,000 |
| Expiry break-even per share | US$687.81 | US$598.12 |
| Maximum option loss if SPY reaches zero | US$68,781 | US$598,120 |
| Premium / full assignment obligation | 1.7414% | 0.3133% |

Chart: pair gross premium bars with separate assignment-obligation bars. Use separate labelled axes so the additional US$661 premium is not visually confused with the additional US$530,000 obligation.

sections.heading: What the comparison means
sections.body:
Strategy A was an ownership-oriented illustration; Strategy B was a leveraged premium-harvesting illustration. The first structure requires willingness and funding to buy 100 shares at the strike. The ten-put structure can create a US$600,000 purchase obligation even when the initial buying-power requirement is much lower.

The reported tenor for Strategy B was 58 days, not roughly 40 days. Preserve the 31 December 2026 expiry and the ticket's displayed day count. Do not compare the two premiums as though they were earned over the same period.

sections.heading: Visual 2: Downside payoff table
sections.body:
| SPY at each option's own expiry | Strategy A P/L | Strategy B P/L |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| US$700 | +US$1,219 | +US$1,880 |
| US$650 | -US$3,781 | +US$1,880 |
| US$600 | -US$8,781 | +US$1,880 |
| US$550 | -US$13,781 | -US$48,120 |
| US$500 | -US$18,781 | -US$98,120 |

Chart: labelled payoff lines, with an explicit warning that the expiries differ. These are terminal scenarios, not interim option marks.

sections.heading: Risks and limits
sections.body:
Buying-power effect is not maximum loss and is not guaranteed to remain fixed. A fall in SPY or a rise in implied volatility can increase short-option losses and margin demands before expiry. Early assignment and forced liquidation are possible.

All returns are conditional and before costs. The original quote reference was SPY US$751.96. The assumed limit premiums do not prove that either trade filled. The report makes no claim about current availability, current pricing or personal account balances.

report.title: QQQ hedge update: partial protection through a sharper selloff
report.period_basis: Historical option snapshot and scenario analysis
report.provenance: Approved redacted summary of the dated private report. Original account evidence is not published.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: The working eight-put example showed an indicative gain of US$14,216, not a confirmed trading profit. The analysis used eight QQQ US$750 puts expiring 19 February 2027, a reconstructed reference premium of US$46.50 and the later displayed bid of US$64.27. Entry and exit fills were not established.

sections.heading: Visual 1: Three-stage quote and valuation table
sections.body:
| Measure | Initial reference | 30 October review | 31 October update |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| QQQ snapshot | US$721.25 | US$715.28 | US$690.53 |
| Put premium per share | US$46.50 reconstructed | US$51.96 bid | US$64.27 bid |
| Eight-contract value | US$37,200 | US$41,568 | US$51,416 |
| Conditional gain | US$0 | +US$4,368 | +US$14,216 |

Chart: use three separate labelled observations, not a continuous live-price series. Reference cost is reconstructed; later values are indicative bid-side marks.

sections.heading: Purpose and outcome
sections.body:
The plan was temporary protection through an earnings window, with an intended exit one week after entry. A longer option expiry was chosen to reduce estimated short-holding-period time decay. The stated purpose was protection against a repricing associated with AI capital spending, cash-flow pressure and debt-service concerns, rather than a claim that a particular company would fail.

The later update showed a larger dollar gain but a smaller proportion of the illustrative stock loss offset. The report's QQQ-equivalent portfolio comparison showed 47.68% of the reference loss offset, versus 75.39% in the earlier review. Actual stock holdings and their returns were not established.

sections.heading: Visual 2: Normalized hedge comparison
sections.body:
Normalize the stock sleeve to 100 reference units. Fund the option premium separately at 5.3143 units, so both cases start with 105.3143 total units.

| At the 31 October snapshot | Without hedge | With the assumed puts |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Stock-sleeve change | -4.2593 units | -4.2593 units |
| Hedge contribution | 0.0000 units | +2.0309 units |
| Combined change | -4.2593 units | -2.2284 units |
| Stock loss offset | 0.00% | 47.68% |

Chart: two loss bars, with the hedge contribution shown as a green bridge. Label this a normalized hypothetical portfolio, not personal account performance.

sections.heading: Costs and limitations
sections.body:
Time decay was one component of cost, not a fixed insurance bill. Starting Greeks suggested approximately US$660 of seven-day theta for the eight-put example if price and implied volatility were unchanged. Price moves, volatility changes, bid-ask spreads and execution costs could produce very different results.

These snapshots do not establish a completed one-week hedge or a realized return. The latest midpoint would imply a US$14,908 gain, but midpoint is not an assured fill. Fees, financing, dividends, tax and slippage are excluded, and a QQQ proxy cannot establish the performance of a different stock portfolio.
